title: SSYS Extension
description: STAC Solar System Extension for STAC Items, Catalogs, and Collections.

ssys:local_time.description: Local solar time at the observation target.

ssys:targets.description: List of solar system targets relevant to the data.

ssys:north_azimuth.description:
The angle between a line from the image center to the north pole and a horizontal reference line from the image center to the middle of the right edge, increasing clockwise, with the image displayed according to its declared display direction. Range: 0–360°.
Source: NASA PDS4 Data Dictionary, geom:north_azimuth (class Object_Orientation_North_East), https://pds.nasa.gov/datastandards/documents/dd/v1/PDS4_PDS_DD_1Q00/ch37s119.html

ssys:solar_longitude.description:
The angle between the body–Sun line at the time of interest and the body–Sun line at its vernal equinox, giving a measure of the season on the target body. Range: 0–360°.
Source: NASA PDS4 Data Dictionary, pds:solar_longitude (class Time_Coordinates), https://pds.nasa.gov/datastandards/documents/dd/v1/PDS4_PDS_DD_1Q00/ch05s840.html

ssys:local_true_solar_time.description:
The local time on a rotating body, equal to 12 h at the subsolar point and increasing by 1 h for every 15° of east longitude away from it, for prograde rotation. In ssys: decimal hours, range 0–24 (PDS4 uses a string).
Source: NASA PDS4 Data Dictionary, pds:local_true_solar_time (class Time_Coordinates), https://pds.nasa.gov/datastandards/documents/dd/v1/PDS4_PDS_DD_1Q00/ch05s438.html

ssys:emission_angle.description:
The angle between the surface normal vector at the intercept point and a vector from the intercept point to the spacecraft. It varies from 0° when the spacecraft is viewing the subspacecraft point (nadir viewing) to 90° when the intercept is tangent to the surface of the target body; higher values indicate more oblique viewing. For ring data, values from 90 to 180° indicate viewing on the unlit side, from oblique or edge-on at 90° to the unlit nadir at 180°. Range: 0–180°.
Source: NASA PDS4 Data Dictionary, geom:emission_angle (class Derived_Geometry), https://pds.nasa.gov/datastandards/documents/dd/v1/PDS4_PDS_DD_1Q00/ch37s34.html

ssys:incidence_angle.description:
A measure of the lighting condition at the intercept point: the angle between the local vertical at the intercept point (surface) and a vector from the intercept point to the Sun. It varies from 0° when the intercept point coincides with the subsolar point to 90° when the intercept point is at the terminator; values above 90° correspond to the shadowed or dark portion of the target body. Range: 0–180°.
Source: NASA PDS4 Data Dictionary, geom:incidence_angle (class Derived_Geometry), https://pds.nasa.gov/datastandards/documents/dd/v1/PDS4_PDS_DD_1Q00/ch37s48.html

ssys:phase_angle.description:
A measure of the relationship between the instrument viewing position and incident illumination (such as solar light). Measured at the target, it is the angle between a vector to the illumination source and a vector to the instrument. If illumination is from behind the instrument, the phase angle is small. Range: 0–180°.
Source: NASA PDS4 Data Dictionary, geom:phase_angle (class Illumination_Specific), https://pds.nasa.gov/datastandards/documents/dd/v1/PDS4_PDS_DD_1Q00/ch37s121.html

ssys:sub_solar_azimuth.description:
The angle between the line from the center of an image to the subsolar point on the target and a horizontal reference line (in the image plane) extending from the image center to the middle right edge of the image, increasing clockwise. Range: 0–360°.
Source: NASA PDS4 Data Dictionary, geom:subsolar_azimuth (class Surface_Geometry_Specific), https://pds.nasa.gov/datastandards/documents/dd/v1/PDS4_PDS_DD_1Q00/ch37s203.html

ssys:sub_solar_latitude.description:
The planetocentric latitude of the subsolar point on the target. Range: −90 to 90°.
Source: NASA PDS4 Data Dictionary, geom:subsolar_latitude (class Surface_Geometry_Specific), https://pds.nasa.gov/datastandards/documents/dd/v1/PDS4_PDS_DD_1Q00/ch37s204.html

ssys:sub_solar_longitude.description:
The planetocentric longitude of the subsolar point on the target. Range: 0–360°.
Source: NASA PDS4 Data Dictionary, geom:subsolar_longitude (class Surface_Geometry_Specific), https://pds.nasa.gov/datastandards/documents/dd/v1/PDS4_PDS_DD_1Q00/ch37s205.html

ssys:sub_spacecraft_latitude.description:
The planetocentric latitude of the sub-spacecraft point on the target. Range: −90 to 90°.
Source: NASA PDS4 Data Dictionary, geom:subspacecraft_latitude (class Surface_Geometry_Specific), https://pds.nasa.gov/datastandards/documents/dd/v1/PDS4_PDS_DD_1Q00/ch37s207.html

ssys:sub_spacecraft_longitude.description:
The planetocentric longitude of the sub-spacecraft point on the target. Range: 0–360°.
Source: NASA PDS4 Data Dictionary, geom:subspacecraft_longitude (class Surface_Geometry_Specific), https://pds.nasa.gov/datastandards/documents/dd/v1/PDS4_PDS_DD_1Q00/ch37s208.html
